description: Semantic knowledge base for Quality Attribute classification in DesignTrace AI.

attributes.name: Security
attributes.definition: The degree to which a software system protects information, assets, and transactions so that persons or systems have the degree of data access appropriate to their authorization, preventing unauthorized disclosure, tampering, or malicious compromise.
representative_descriptions: Cryptographic protection, encryption of sensitive data in transit and at rest, and secure credential handling.
Role-based access control, fine-grained permission authorization, and identity verification.
Tamper-proof audit logging, digital signatures, compliance with privacy standards like HIPAA and GDPR.
Protection against unauthorized intrusion, code injection, and data exfiltration.
positive_examples: All transactions must be strictly audited with cryptographic tamper protection and role-based access control.
Medical records access must comply with HIPAA, maintaining complete data confidentiality and tamper-proof audit trails.
All user passwords and payment credentials must be encrypted using salted hashes and transmitted strictly over TLS 1.3.
The system must enforce multi-factor authentication and revoke sessions after 15 minutes of inactivity.
Sensitive customer identifiers must be anonymized before being written to diagnostic logs.
architectural_indicators: Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) and certificate managers
OAuth2, OpenID Connect, and JWT authentication tokens
Cryptographic envelope encryption and HSM integration
Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) and Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) interceptors
Tamper-evident append-only audit ledgers

attributes.name: Scalability
attributes.definition: The ability of a system to handle growing amounts of work, user traffic, or transaction volume gracefully by adding computing resources horizontally or vertically without software architectural redesign.
representative_descriptions: Handling massive bursts in concurrent client requests, high-throughput streaming events, and expanding datasets.
Horizontal scaling across multiple compute instances, nodes, or distributed worker pools.
Elastic compute provisioning and load distribution across replicated services.
Decoupled asynchronous processing pipelines preventing bottlenecks under high load.
positive_examples: The platform shall ingest and process up to 50,000 checkout events per second during peak flash sales.
The telemetry gateway shall ingest sensor time-series packets from 250,000 edge devices with under 100ms processing latency.
The architecture must scale out dynamically to support a ten-fold increase in daily active users during promotional campaigns.
Batch data ingestion must scale linearly as dataset size expands from gigabytes to terabytes.
The system must partition order storage across database shards to support exponential transaction growth.
architectural_indicators: Horizontal autoscaling groups and container orchestration
Message queuing systems (Kafka, RabbitMQ, SQS)
Database sharding and read-replica distribution
Partitioned streaming event topics and consumer groups
Decoupled microservice and asynchronous event-driven topologies

attributes.name: Performance
attributes.definition: The degree to which a system accomplishes its designated functions within specified constraints regarding time behavior, processing latency, throughput, and resource utilization efficiency.
representative_descriptions: Sub-second round-trip latency, rapid response times, and fast computational turnarounds.
High transaction throughput and optimized input/output processing speed.
Low-latency caching strategies and query execution optimization.
Efficient computational resource utilization under continuous workload.
positive_examples: The system must return search results to end-users in under 200 milliseconds under normal operating conditions.
The telemetry gateway shall ingest sensor time-series packets from 250,000 edge devices with under 100ms processing latency.
The payment verification service must process authorization callbacks within 500 milliseconds.
Database queries for product catalog views must execute in less than 50 milliseconds via memory caches.
Video transcoding pipelines must achieve a processing rate of 60 frames per second without frame drops.
architectural_indicators: In-memory distributed caches (Redis, Memcached)
Content Delivery Networks (CDNs) and edge caching
Asynchronous non-blocking I/O event loops
Optimized query indexes and read-optimized denormalization
Connection pooling and compression pipelines

attributes.name: Reliability
attributes.definition: The ability of a system or component to perform its required functions under stated conditions for a specified period of time, ensuring fault tolerance, error resilience, and graceful failure isolation.
representative_descriptions: Fault isolation preventing cascading system failures across interdependent components.
Resilient error recovery, circuit breaking, retry strategies, and deterministic rollback.
Transactional consistency guarantees and data durability despite unexpected node crashes.
Self-healing architecture and graceful degradation during partial component outages.
positive_examples: Payment processing failures must be isolated and not halt inventory or order capture streams.
Financial statements must enforce deterministic consistency and rollback capabilities on failure.
The system must employ circuit breakers to isolate failing third-party APIs without crashing the core workflow.
Unacknowledged queue messages must be automatically retried with exponential backoff before routing to a dead-letter queue.
Critical temperature warning events must be immediately broadcasted to alerting services asynchronously without dropped packets.
architectural_indicators: Circuit breakers, fallback handlers, and bulkhead isolation patterns
Dead-letter queues and automated idempotent retries
Saga pattern for distributed transactional consistency and compensating actions
Active-passive redundancy and automated failover detection
Idempotent consumer patterns ensuring exactly-once semantic processing

attributes.name: Maintainability
attributes.definition: The degree of effectiveness and efficiency with which a system can be modified, repaired, enhanced, adapted, or evolved by developers, featuring clean separation of concerns, modularity, and testability.
representative_descriptions: High modularity, low component coupling, and strong internal cohesion.
Ease of software maintenance, code readability, refactoring flexibility, and clean architecture boundaries.
Extensibility for future plugins or domain features without rewriting core components.
Clear module boundaries allowing small development teams to evolve services independently.
positive_examples: The portal shall be easily maintainable by a small 3-person developer team with minimal operational complexity.
New employee profile modules and payroll reporting plugins must be modularly extendable without full re-architecture.
The codebase must adhere to clean architecture layering so database technologies can be replaced without modifying business logic.
Core pricing calculations must be isolated into a standalone domain module to facilitate unit testing and frequent rule changes.
External integrations must be encapsulated behind adapter interfaces to prevent third-party SDK changes from breaking core code.
architectural_indicators: Layered / Hexagonal / Ports-and-Adapters architecture
Dependency injection and interface segregation
Domain-Driven Design (DDD) bounded contexts
Modular monolith component boundaries
Automated unit and integration test harnesses with high testability

attributes.name: Availability
attributes.definition: The proportion of time that a system is in an operational state, accessible, and functioning properly when required for use, characterized by minimal downtime, continuous operation, and automated disaster failover.
representative_descriptions: Continuous 24/7 system uptime and elimination of single points of failure.
High availability SLAs such as 99.9% or 99.999% uptime for mission-critical operations.
Automated health checks, redundant multi-zone replication, and rapid disaster failover.
Zero-downtime rolling deployments and hot standby operational failovers.
positive_examples: The vital sign alerting subsystem must guarantee 99.999% uptime and zero single points of failure.
The online store checkout portal must maintain 99.95% continuous operational availability throughout the holiday quarter.
The platform must support zero-downtime blue/green rolling deployments during regular business hours.
Database clusters must replicate across multi-region availability zones with automated sub-second failover.
Health check endpoints must automatically remove unhealthy container instances from the load balancer pool.
architectural_indicators: Multi-region active-active or active-standby replication
Global server load balancers and automated health probing
Elimination of single points of failure (SPOF)
Zero-downtime deployment pipelines (Canary, Blue/Green)
Automatic database clustering with distributed consensus (Raft/Paxos)
